Receive proactive suggestions: From sharing your ETA with a tap when someone asks when you’ll arrive, to helping you find the perfect dinner spot, your Pixel anticipates what you need with timely information and suggested actions, so you can accomplish your daily tasks faster. 1 Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4. Create more personalized widgets: Ever find yourself wanting a widget that doesn’t seem to exist? Create personalized widgets, like a tracker to follow your monthly spending, a game day widget with your team colors, or a getaway countdown that automatically pulls in flight and reservation details. Your home screen can be as personalized as you want it to be. Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5. 2 Catch up on long conversations: Your Pixel can now provide summaries of your longer conversations, so you can see what’s important right away. Now available in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Hindi, and Traditional Chinese. Coming to Pixel Watches soon. 3 Call Screen got an upgrade on Pixel 11 series Whenever you see a call from an unknown number and choose to screen it, Gemini will ask unknown callers why they're reaching out in a much more conversational manner handling the exchange until you decide to jump in or end the call. With a live transcript displayed right on your screen, you can easily follow along and decide exactly when to pick up. Also, coming to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 soon. 4 Personalize your Pixel with new custom icon styles Following the launch of Custom Icons earlier this year, we’re adding more styles to give you even more ways to personalize your home screen Pixel. Pick from distinct styles that apply across all your app icons on the home screen. 5 New updates coming to Pixel search Now available on Pixel 6 and newer devices, Pixel search helps you find what you need across your phone – from vacation photos and recent emails to messages, calendar events, and device settings. 6 Stay in the moment with Google Messages and HiLight HiLight now supports Google Messages. When your phone is face down, HiLight will glow if you receive a message from one of your favorite contacts — letting you stay present without missing important messages or calls. 7 Keep tabs on your belongings with Pixel Tag Pixel Tag offers peace of mind so you always know where your most important things are — and it’s available November 11. It’s slim enough to fit in your wallet and durable enough to attach to your belongings, with a battery that lasts over a year. The Find Hub network of more than 1 billion Android devices helps you locate your belongings even if they are miles away and UWB enables visual direction and distance guidance to find it nearby. 8 Pixel Tag is available starting November 11 for $29.99 for one or $99.99 for a four-pack. Switch between two of America's best 5G networks with Google Fi Starting today on eligible Pixels, Google Fi’s new super network delivers the nation's fastest, most expansive coverage by automatically switching between two of America's top 5G cellular networks and millions of secure Wi-Fi networks. 9 10 11 12 Already have a Pixel but not using Google Fi? Get 50% off on select unlimited plans for 12 months. Ends 12/1/26. All terms apply. Visit the blog post , Google Fi website for details, and join Google Fi today . Related Article Google Fi’s new super network Google Fi Wireless is launching a new super network, combining two 5G networks with millions of Wi-Fi networks in one phone plan. See more Unlock your Pixel Watch with your phone Your Pixel devices work better together. When your watch is on your wrist and you’ve unlocked your nearby phone, your Pixel Watch will automatically unlock so you can skip typing your PIN or pattern on the watch. Coming in the next few weeks. 13 Step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch We’re now rolling out step-by-step workouts to Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. Whether you’re following an exercise routine created by your Google Health Coach 14 or a custom workout built in the Google Health app, you can get step-by-step instructions, log reps and weights, and track metrics directly from your Pixel Watch or your phone. title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
body: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices Nov 10, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Gemini Intelligence is now available on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10. See how expanded capabilities across these devices help you do more. Karthik Thirumalai Product Director, Android AI Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Gemini Intelligence 1 brings the best of Gemini to Android devices, helping your devices work harder for you. Earlier this year, we announced Gemini Intelligence , and this summer devices started rolling out — from the Pixel 11 to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Flip8 and S26 series. 2 Today, we’re introducing new features built for Gemini Intelligence, and expanding capabilities to more of Android’s most advanced devices . 3 Here’s a look at what’s new. Gemini Intelligence on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10 Gemini Intelligence is coming to even more devices. Motorola is introducing its first Gemini Intelligence device, motorola signature 27 , which is available for pre-order in the U.S. on November 19. And with today’s Pixel Drop , Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold get the latest features for Gemini Intelligence. Alongside this expansion, we’re bringing some of our favorite capabilities to more devices and regions, helping handle the busywork so you can focus on what matters. Rambler 4 — which turns spoken thoughts into clean, organized text in real-time — is now available on Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10, Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold, as well as the new motorola signature 27. And task automation 5 — which lets you ask Gemini to handle logistics like ordering food, hailing rides, or booking reservations across your favorite apps — is expanding to the UK, India, and Japan. title: Get step-by-step workout guidance on your Pixel Watch.
body: Get step-by-step workout guidance on your Pixel Watch. Anna Bernbaum Product Manager, Fitbit Nov 10, 2026 Step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch 3 and newer models, starting today. This feature, first announced with the launch of Pixel Watch 5, provides live guidance on your watch during each exercise in your workout. Whether you’re following a personalized workout from the Google Health Coach 1 or a custom exercise routine manually built in the Google Health app, you can view step-by-step instructions on your Pixel Watch or on your phone. Lane Member of the ECB's Executive Board SPEECH The science and practice of monetary policy communication: the ECB experience Keynote speech by Philip R. Lane, Member of the Executive Board of the ECB, at the Bank of England and its Watchers Conference London, 10 November 2026 Monetary policy is about more than just the latest interest rate decision. It also involves communication about future economic developments and the factors shaping future policy decisions. [ 1 ] By steering the expectations of financial market participants, central bank communication shapes the full set of financial market prices across the maturity and risk spectrums, in turn affecting financing conditions and decisions around credit, saving and investment. The decisions of households and firms are also affected by their beliefs about monetary policy, which depend on how the central bank communicates. [ 2 ] I will divide this speech into two parts. In the first part, I will review recent contributions by ECB staff on the science of monetary policy communication. [ 3 ] In the second part, I will discuss the practice of monetary policy communication from an ECB perspective. The science of monetary policy communication Greater data availability, increased computing power and artificial intelligence have substantially expanded the tools available for analysing central bank communication. Until recently, researchers relied on dictionary-based approaches to quantify the content and tone of monetary policy statements and speeches. This involved categorising specific words and expressions associated with a restrictive or accommodative stance, or with different assessments of inflation and the economic outlook. [ 4 ] Machine learning techniques and large language models (LLMs) now allow for the extensive analysis of large volumes of text in a more automated manner, taking into account the context in which words are used instead of relying solely on the frequency of individual words or predefined expressions. [ 5 ] Recent ECB research illustrates these possibilities. A set of novel, LLM-based in-house measures of the tone of ECB monetary policy communication confirms that it becomes more hawkish during tightening phases and more dovish during easing periods. These shifts in communication closely track developments in the deposit facility rate (Chart 1, panel a). [ 6 ] The importance of communication is also illustrated by the research finding that information extracted from ECB monetary policy statements can improve forecasts of euro area core inflation several quarters ahead, even when controlling for the contributions of Eurosystem and ECB staff projections. [ 7 ] These indicators can also be employed to test whether central bank communication follows systematic patterns that reflect the economic outlook and the policy stance. Indeed, the evidence suggests that central banks tend to communicate in a systematic manner, following “communication rules”. [ 8 ] By estimating a systematic relationship between the tone of communication on monetary policy, economic activity and inflation, ECB staff find that, in line with our primary objective of price stability, ECB communication on monetary policy systematically places more emphasis on inflation developments (Chart 1, panel b). These new tools therefore provide valuable insights into aspects of communication that conventional financial market indicators may not fully capture. At the same time, their use requires careful validation, since the results depend on how questions are formulated and what data are used for training. Financial markets Financial market participants closely follow central bank communication because it provides information about both the economic and inflation outlook and the expected path of monetary policy. Both of these dimensions are relevant for asset pricing and investment decisions. Central bank communication can influence interest rate expectations and financial conditions, independently from actual policy changes. [ 10 ] Research shows that financial analysts reassess the monetary policy stance following ECB Governing Council announcements, considering both the policy decision and the accompanying communication. Unexpected revisions in their assessment contain information beyond conventional market-based monetary policy surprises and are associated with significant effects on economic and financial conditions. For instance, even when an interest rate decision is widely anticipated and generates little immediate market reaction, the accompanying communication may lead market analysts to reassess how restrictive is monetary policy or how it is likely to evolve. The importance of communication extends beyond Governing Council meetings. Research examining thousands of speeches, interviews, hearings and other events shows that communication in the time period between meetings can affect market interest rates across maturities. It can help markets anticipate policy changes, particularly ahead of tightening episodes, and its cumulative effect over time can be comparable to that of policy announcements, especially at longer maturities (Chart 2). The tone of ECB communication can influence monetary policy uncertainty and premia on risky assets. [ 13 ] In particular, financial markets respond to several dimensions of monetary policy news: the current policy rate, the expected path of rates, and market and sovereign risk (“target”, “path”, and “risk” in Chart 3, respectively). Households and firms Communicating with households and firms presents different challenges to communicating with markets. Unlike professional market participants, most households do not closely follow central bank communication. And even when they do encounter central bank messages, they may interpret their implications differently to market analysts. Research presented in our 2021 monetary policy strategy review suggests that information about the new inflation target reached only around one in ten consumers in the months following its announcement. Most learned about the new inflation target through television, radio and newspapers rather than directly from the ECB (Chart 4). Attention to inflation varies with the economic environment. When inflation is high, households and firms tend to pay more attention, while they pay less attention when inflation is low and stable (Chart 5). [ 15 ] This matters for the transmission of monetary policy. What households and firms believe about future inflation, and how confident they are that the central bank will deliver price stability, shapes how they set wages and prices and how they adjust their spending and saving when we change interest rates. [ 16 ] When inflation is high, households tend to be more attentive, but they may also be less responsive to information they already know. This underscores the importance of tailoring communication to the economic environment to ensure that messages reach households when inflation is low while providing clear, relevant and informative explanations when inflation becomes more salient. [ 17 ] Households typically interpret monetary policy in terms of how it directly affects their economic circumstances. Euro area consumers tend to associate monetary policy primarily with borrowing costs rather than directly with inflation. Those who emphasise the borrowing-cost channel may also respond more strongly to a rate rise in their planned spending decisions. [ 18 ] The expectations of firms are also important for monetary policy transmission. Their views about future inflation influence pricing, wage-setting and investment decisions, and ultimately the evolution of inflation itself. Recent evidence shows that attention paid by firms to inflation varies considerably over time, increasing when inflationary pressures become more pronounced (Chart 5, panel b). The estimation sample is from 2002-25. It is also important to recognise that monetary policy announcements convey different types of information. Markets respond not only to the decision, but also to what it reveals about the assessment of the economy. A surprise rate rise may signal tighter policy, but it may also lead markets to reassess the strength of activity or the persistence of inflation. Research has developed methods to separate policy surprises from the so-called central bank information effects, and more recently from surprises about how the central bank responds to publicly available news. These distinctions are important in order to assess accurately the effects of monetary policy communication. [ 20 ] Recent research shows that these channels are distinct and can be identified together, which sharpens estimates of how policy affects the economy. [ 21 ] For the ECB, research finds that estimated monetary policy surprises on meeting days – the movements in interest rates in a narrow window around the announcement – are partially inferable from euro area equity market changes over the six weeks preceding the meeting. [ 22 ] Market reactions to speeches, by contrast, show no such pattern. [ 23 ] Information conveyed by ECB announcements also travels across borders. The evidence suggests that it accounts for an important part of the co-movement of German and US government bond yields around ECB announcement days. [ 24 ] ECB staff have also analysed the implications of uncertainty for monetary policy communication. When economic conditions are changing rapidly, it may be preferable to place greater emphasis on the current state of the economy than on precise indications about the distant future. [ 25 ] The appropriate degree of precision also depends on how confident policymakers are in their forecasts and how that confidence is perceived. [ 26 ] Moreover, how policymakers express confidence in their assessment – or acknowledge developments that differ from expectations – can itself be informative about the policy stance. [ 27 ] Trust and credibility Finally, economic agents need to not only clearly understand central bank messages but also trust that the words will be followed by action. Explaining why the ECB’s inflation target matters for economic stability can strengthen public confidence in our commitment to keep prices stable. Such explanations are particularly effective among people with lower financial literacy, as they can help them understand how monetary policy contributes to achieving the inflation target. The effects can persist for several months but tend to fade over time. [ 28 ] Building and maintaining credibility therefore requires more than communicating individual decisions clearly. It requires explaining, consistently and repeatedly, why our objective matters and how our policies contribute to achieving it. [ 29 ] The practice of monetary policy communication Having reviewed recent scientific research on monetary policy communication in the first part of this speech, I will now turn to a discussion of monetary policy communication in practice. Throughout its history, the ECB has adapted its communication content to changes in the economy, the instruments activated in setting the monetary policy stance and the nature of the uncertainty facing policymakers (Chart 7). Before the global financial crisis, ECB monetary policy communication focused on explaining decisions and making the underlying reaction function more predictable, without explicitly signalling an interest rate path. [ 30 ] Since its inception, the ECB has held press conferences to accompany its policy decisions. The publication of staff macroeconomic projections from 2004 onwards provided further information about the outlook. Policy decisions were systematically related to the assessment of risks surrounding the projected inflation path, while communication between meetings could help markets anticipate turning points. For instance, the speech by ECB President Trichet on 18 November 2005 ahead of the December 2005 interest rate increase helped prepare markets for the first interest rate increase in five years. [ 31 ] Through these steps, news about the orientation of monetary policy influenced medium- and longer-term yields even before the era of explicit forward guidance. [ 32 ] The global financial crisis and the euro area sovereign debt crisis fundamentally changed the environment. Amid severe financial stress, effective communication played an essential role in restoring confidence and supporting smooth monetary policy transmission. This was particularly evident in the summer of 2012 due to rising financial fragmentation and elevated sovereign risk premia. The ECB's commitment to do “whatever it takes” to preserve the euro, followed by the announcement of the Outright Monetary Transactions (OMT) instrument, helped alleviate these concerns and contributed to a substantial decline in sovereign bond yields and narrowing spreads in the countries most affected by the crisis. This episode illustrates how communication backed by a clear policy commitment can safeguard smooth monetary policy transmission. [ 33 ] As policy rates approached the effective lower bound, influencing expectations about future rates became all the more important. The ECB introduced explicit rate forward guidance in July 2013. By communicating on the future policy path, rate forward guidance sought to influence market expectations and financing conditions beyond the immediate policy horizon. Experience showed that design matters. Longer-horizon and state-contingent guidance can reduce uncertainty about future rates by clarifying the conditions under which policy may change. By contrast, short-horizon or open-ended guidance may be less effective and can even increase uncertainty if it leaves markets unsure about the central bank's future course of action. [ 34 ] The interaction with other instruments matters as well. Asset purchases can reinforce the effectiveness of forward guidance, while clear information about the scale of purchase programmes can reduce uncertainty. However, linking the sequencing of asset purchases to interest rate decisions can also constrain policy flexibility when economic conditions change unexpectedly. As a result of the 2021 monetary policy strategy review, the Governing Council adopted the symmetric two per cent inflation target. At the following monetary policy meeting (July 2021), it revised its rate forward guidance by linking the expected policy path more explicitly to the inflation outlook and realised progress in underlying inflation. This reinforced the commitment to a forceful or persistent monetary policy response aimed at achieving the inflation target when inflation appeared at risk of undershooting the target. [ 35 ] [ 36 ] However, in the wake of the 2021-2022 inflation surge, the guidance that had been designed specifically for an environment of persistently below-target inflation was no longer appropriate. The period between July 2022 and March 2023 constituted an important transition phase. In July 2022 the Governing Council moved away from the effective lower bound by raising the policy rate from minus 50 basis points to zero. [ 37 ] In line with the 2021 strategy decision that the ECB key interest rates are the primary monetary policy instrument away from the effective lower bound, the monetary policy statement did not provide specific guidance on the expected future rate path. However, it did provide directional guidance, indicating that further rate normalisation would be appropriate at upcoming meetings, even if the exact calibration would be data-dependent and decided on a meeting-by-meeting basis. The following four meetings (September 2022 to February 2023) maintained directional guidance, with a pair of 75 basis point hikes followed by a pair of 50 basis point hikes. In addition, the February 2023 meeting articulated the intention to also hike by 50 basis points at the March meeting, which was subsequently implemented. However, having quickly raised the policy rate from -50 to 300 between July 2022 and March 2023, the March 2023 monetary policy statement replaced directional guidance with the reaction function guidance that future interest rate decisions would be based on the inflation outlook in light of incoming economic and financial data, underlying inflation dynamics and the strength of monetary policy transmission. These criteria would be assessed on a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting basis. These elements of the reaction function remain in place. An explicit role for the risks surrounding the inflation outlook was added in July 2025: this reflected one implementation of the conclusion of the 2025 monetary policy strategy assessment that monetary policy decisions should explicitly incorporate this risk assessment. Although it turned out that the following four meetings would also deliver hikes (25 basis points at each meeting, bringing the policy rate to 400 basis points), there was a clear gear shift at the March 2023 meeting. In essence, after a series of rapid and outsized hikes, the gap between the policy rate and the plausible range of the “appropriate level” of the policy rate was no longer so wide as to justify ongoing formal directional guidance. [ 38 ] While formal directional guidance may be appropriate in the early phases of a forceful monetary policy response to a large inflation shock in either direction, it may convey an excessive level of certainty about the future rate path in the later phases (after a large adjustment has already been put in place). Similarly, avoiding formal directional guidance is prudent in implementing a measured monetary policy response to less extreme inflation shocks. [ 39 ] The framework guidance provided by the Governing Council can be interpreted as implementing the strategic approach to making monetary policy decisions that was laid out in the 2021 monetary policy strategy statement. [ 40 ] In particular, the 2021 strategy committed to basing monetary policy decisions on an integrated assessment of all relevant factors, taking into account the interdependencies between the economic analysis of real and nominal variables and the monetary and financial analysis that focused on the monetary transmission mechanism. Since it would be unwise to rely exclusively on inflation projections, especially during times of high uncertainty, a balanced approach that takes into account both the forward-looking inflation outlook and the information revealed by the realised path of underlying inflation is preferable, with underlying inflation indicators distilling the realised inflation data to uncover the components most relevant for the medium term. In calibrating monetary policy, it is also essential to rely on the latest assessment of the strength of monetary transmission, given the range of uncertainty about the timing and strength of the macro-financial impact of shifts in the monetary policy stance and the scope for exogenous shocks to financial conditions and financing conditions. [ 41 ] Framework guidance delivers a systematic approach to monetary policy that is interpretable by financial market participants and external experts. The 2021 monetary policy strategy statement highlighted that monetary policy decisions are communicated through the monetary policy statement, the press conference, the Economic Bulletin and the monetary policy accounts. Together with the publication of the quarterly staff macroeconomic projections exercises, these releases provide the analytical underpinnings of how the reaction function criteria are assessed. Further analysis is provided through staff working papers and contributions to the ECB Blog, along with presentations and speeches by ECB Executive Board members. [ 42 ] Recent ECB research shows that the sensitivity of rate expectations to macroeconomic news appears to have increased under the ECB’s current framework guidance regime compared with the period of explicit forward guidance, where short-term rates were mostly constrained by an effective lower bound, implying a smaller information content of surprises for the expected policy path (Chart 8). Markets seem to have incorporated macroeconomic news in rate expectations in a systematic manner only after the explicit formulation of the reaction function criteria, which also came at a time of receding macroeconomic uncertainty. That said, the evidence is suggestive rather than conclusive: the economic environment, the degree of uncertainty and the constraints facing monetary policy also changed substantially between those periods. Nevertheless, it highlights how communication frameworks can influence expectations and the transmission of monetary policy. Finally, incorporating uncertainty into monetary policy communication poses trade-offs. [ 43 ] In view of the high level of external trust in the systematic and comprehensive analysis that underpin the exercise, the information anchor provided by the baseline projections is more valuable than ever in an environment of elevated uncertainty. At the same time, in relation to specific and material risk events, the publication of alternative scenarios can help financial markets, experts and the public understand the possible quantitative impact on inflation and growth dynamics if these alternative scenarios were to materialise. [ 44 ] A communication risk is that excessive focus in placed on the published scenarios rather than also taking into account the comprehensive risk assessment that is contained in each monetary policy statement and expanded upon in the accounts. During any period, a range of risk factors can materialise, such that a wide-angled perspective is needed, rather than taking a reductive approach that overly focuses on any particular set of scenarios. [ 45 ] Conclusions In this speech, I have outlined some recent ECB research on the science of monetary policy communication. In particular, I have highlighted that new text-based tools, including large language models, allow us to measure central bank communication more systematically, and these confirm that what we say moves financial markets, between meetings as well as on meeting days. Relative to markets-orientated communication, reaching households and firms is more challenging: their attention to inflation rises and falls with inflation itself, which makes clear and consistent communication even more important when inflation is elevated. In relation to the practice of monetary policy communication, framework guidance is more effective than rate forward guidance when policy rates are away from the effective lower bound. In particular, framework guidance retains the beneficial properties of forward guidance in providing an anchor for rate expectations without incurring the costs in terms of inflexibility and the risk of misperceptions. By communicating a reaction function that spells out the criteria that guide our decisions, our framework guidance has helped markets interpret the incoming data. Clarity and consistency are essential to make communication effective, as emphasised by the findings of both the ECB's 2021 strategy review and the 2025 strategy assessment. Clarity of communication is a prerequisite to ensure that decisions are correctly understood by financial market participants, firms and households, while coherence across messages over time and between words and actions is essential for public trust and central bank credibility. Prior to 2008, the ECB aimed to outline its reaction function through a transparent and structured monetary policy strategy, while deliberately avoiding rigid adherence to simplistic rules. In articulating the approach of the ECB to monetary policy communication, Issing (2000) stressed that “there is no convincing alternative to the arduous task of continuously explaining how we arrive at, confirm or refine our common assessment of the outlook for price stability meeting by meeting, month by month. The ECB practice is to examine alternative scenarios while holding fixed the market interest rate curve. This helps to keep apart the conditional macroeconomic impact of the alternative scenarios from the endogenous monetary policy response. It is not difficult for market participants to explore possible monetary policy responses to alternative scenarios by running policy simulations, especially since the ECB publishes the details of the main macroeconomic models that it uses. title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
body: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure At KubeCon, NVIDIA is putting tools to secure agents and run AI on Kubernetes in the hands of the cloud-native community. November 10, 2026 by Warren Barkley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. Securing AI Agents in the Open NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF puts security infrastructure for autonomous agents in the community’s hands to build, inspect and improve — accelerating development and hardening its safeguards. “The cloud-native community has a new infrastructure challenge: giving agents secure environments in which to operate,” said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. “NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF gives developers a shared foundation to build on and an opportunity to shape how agent security evolves. Bringing this work into the community enables broader collaboration on infrastructure that will be critical to the next generation of cloud-native applications.” OpenShell gives organizations control over what AI agents can do. It applies deterministic controls to agent activity, so teams can enforce policies as agents use tools, access inference services and execute workloads. Its extensible architecture lets teams connect their own compute, inference providers, credential storage and monitoring tools. This allows organizations to apply governance across different deployment environments while integrating OpenShell with their existing enterprise systems. Hundreds of organizations have put OpenShell to use, and the project has received tens of thousands of contributions in less than a year since launch. Scaling Agent Execution on Kubernetes Governing agents is only part of the challenge. Organizations also need to deploy them at scale. NVIDIA is contributing to Agent Substrate, a Google -originated project in the CNCF Sandbox, and ensuring it works with NVIDIA Dynamo for model inference and KAI Scheduler for shared cluster resource allocation. This effort brings together agent execution, inference serving and resource scheduling on Kubernetes. Agent Substrate preserves agent environments between tasks while releasing compute when agents are idle. By suspending and resuming those environments across a shared pool of agents, it lets teams scale agent workloads without keeping dedicated compute running for every session. NVIDIA and Google are also collaborating on an integration of OpenShell and Agent Substrate, so enterprises can secure and govern agents across clouds and on-premises systems. Building an Open Foundation for AI Factories AI factories need to offer customers managed Kubernetes services while retaining control of their infrastructure, software and customer experience. Three new open source projects extend the DSX AI Factory Platform to make Kubernetes easier to run and inference faster to scale. The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform software stack, from GPU infrastructure and Kubernetes management to workload orchestration and model serving. NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) — now available in public preview — provide open source building blocks for delivering managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure. They automate cluster lifecycle management and provide signed, version-pinned images. NVKE and NVKR are launching with ecosystem support that extends their reach across AI infrastructure platforms and cloud services. Mirantis, Netris, OpenNebula Systems, Rafay , Spectro Cloud and vCluster, together with Firmus and SK Telecom , have aligned with NVIDIA on integration plans to bring NVKE and NVKR capabilities into their offerings. NVIDIA Snapshot addresses the challenge of bringing additional inference capacity online quickly. Loading models and warming up workloads can delay scaling and recovery. The open source, modular component restores checkpointed replicas in seconds, without model reload or warmup, supporting faster startup, recovery and elasticity for inference and agentic workloads on Kubernetes. Design partners Crusoe and Saturn Cloud have evaluated Snapshot on their own workloads using NVIDIA HGX B300 systems . Crusoe , an upstream contributor to Snapshot, tested GLM-5.3 on Crusoe Cloud and reduced the time for the workload to become ready from roughly eight minutes to 31 seconds. Saturn Cloud , a token factory platform, benchmarked Snapshot for scale-from-zero inference and reduced vLLM startup times from between two and 8.5 minutes to six and 34 seconds. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at KubeCon . title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
body: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available Nov 10, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers can now try our latest frontier model. Koray Kavukcuoglu SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X In this article Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning. Two weeks ago , we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program . Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon , Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops. Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0 , Perplexity’s WANDR , and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model. To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change. Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, at the same introductory price 1 as Gemini 4 Argon ($2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens). It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , the Gemini app , and AI Mode in Search . Higher-precision knowledge work, artifact generation, and data analysis Across legal, finance, and enterprise operations, Gemini 4 Carbon combines frontier visual understanding, reasoning, and exhaustive retrieval to synthesize grounded insights across large sets of dense documents and data. It follows strict schemas and formatting to generate polished and precise spreadsheets, presentations, and reports. Existing benchmarks don’t adequately capture how agents reason natively over dense files with charts, images, blueprints, schematics, and tables, so we partnered with Artificial Analysis to launch the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark that tests a model’s multimodal performance in agentic workflows. Carbon ranks #2 while being more than 6X lower in average cost per task compared to the top performing model. Using Google Antigravity’s new /swarm feature, a team of Gemini 4 Carbon agents turned historical photos and engineering plates into an interactive Three.js 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower's 1887–1889 construction from a single prompt. With seven public City Council planning PDFs (206 extracted engineering drawing views) and a single prompt, a multi-agent Carbon team using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature built an interactive 906K-triangle Three.js reconstruction of Google’s Platform 37 office across 10 overnight loops. In Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Carbon built an interactive multiscale textile visualizer based on an academic paper, modeling a virtual-fiber finite element framework with interactive 3D yarn meshes, 110-fiber polar tracking, and dynamic stress-strain curves with minimal prompting. In pre-release evaluations, Carbon matched the performance of the best model tested on deep financial research on Hebbia’s E2E Financial Agentic evaluation, and ranked at the top out of 23 frontier model configurations on Balyasny Asset Management’s General Financial Intelligence benchmark, spanning legal expertise, agentic tool use and execution, coding and data engineering, and perception and context understanding. Improved agentic coding, full stack development, and 3D and UI design Carbon performs exceptionally well on engineering tasks that require multi-agent collaboration like multi-package migrations, cross-subsystem root-cause investigations, and complex architectural redesigns. For web app development, it runs build-and-verify loops, recovers from errors, and checks both its code and the rendered UI to produce complete, working applications. Stronger visual design, spatial reasoning, and attention to environmental detail also carry over to 3D game development and creative coding. Using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature, Carbon built an open-world 3D game where you explore Google’s Mountain View campus as a pelican riding a GBike — coordinating subagents to model 3D assets in Blender from Omni and Nano Banana references, build the browser game in Three.js with WebGL shaders, and pair procedural Web Audio sound effects with Lyria music. Try the live app . Paired with improved front end taste and motion design skills in Google Antigravity, Carbon reimagined the Google Merchandise Store in two prompts, proposing five art direction concepts and generating all-new product imagery with Nano Banana 2.1. Try the live app and Gemini front end design skill . Starting from a video reference generated with Gemini Omni in Google Antigravity, built a cinematic multi-shot underwater Atlantis scene. The pipeline modeled procedural ruins, volumetric caustic lighting, and water simulation in Blender before converting the full environment to Three.js for real-time browser rendering. Using a multi-agent loop in Google Antigravity, Carbon reconstructed a playable c. 1780 Stein-Schule fortepiano with 61-key escapement physics from CAD drawings and X-ray radiographs and placed it in a 3D model of the Royal Conservatory of Music's Koerner Hall in Toronto with seat-specific spatial acoustics. Try the live app . Frontier cybersecurity capabilities Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber delivers our strongest cybersecurity capabilities to date, giving security teams the end-to-end intelligence they need in protecting critical software. When accessed through the Fairwind Program, Carbon leads on key benchmarks across finding (SEC-bench Pro), exploiting (ExploitGym), and patching (CWE-bench v1) vulnerabilities: inspecting software, tracing how flaws can be chained together across systems, and generating verified root-cause patches. Early testers inside and outside of Google are already seeing strong results with Carbon for cyber in practice. In Project Fortify , Google’s autonomous system spanning scanning, triage, and remediation, Carbon hit 100% recall on scanning and 95% precision on triage, on our internal benchmark. On Open Source code repository testing we see an over 25% relative improvement on Argon's already strong recall rate, surfacing previously undetected, real-world logic flaws. Bringing these gains across Google, one of the world’s largest users of open-source software, helps secure both our own systems and the broader ecosystem. Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research (CVR) team recently used Carbon to prove that two bugs in a popular open-source software were in fact exploitable vulnerabilities, comparable in severity to the recent PHP2Shell exploit . By using Carbon to build a proof of concept, CVR helped maintainers re-classify the bug as critical and swiftly issue a patch. Details will be shared after the responsible disclosure process completes. As part of Wiz’s Scan for Good program, the team used Carbon to assess vulnerabilities in public digital infrastructure. For example, when scanning two major SaaS providers, the model uncovered 0-day vulnerabilities in under two hours compressing weeks of vulnerability research to a single afternoon. The team partnered with the impacted organizations to remediate in record time, helping to mitigate potential impact on tens of thousands of companies. Stronger scientific and mathematical reasoning Gemini 4 Carbon shows strongly improved performance in reasoning across physics, math, and life sciences, synthesizing experimental data, testing hypotheses, and reasoning through multi-step domain problems. For drug toxicity research company Axiom Bio, Carbon is now the leading model in performance for translational science, finding novel mechanisms of toxicity they hadn’t found previously. Axiom is now moving their production scientific analyses and agents to both Carbon and Argon to unlock the creation of safer drugs. Researchers across Google have been using Carbon in Google Antigravity to accelerate their work: Code verification: Researchers built a new agentic framework for formal verification called AlphaProof Code and put it to work on a major security challenge: mathematically proving the actual code underlying the cryptographic protocol of Signal . Using Carbon alongside other models, our researchers translated security goals to mathematical theorems. AlphaProof Code agents then used Carbon to generate millions of lines of code in Lean, a computer language for writing mathematical proofs, helping them prove key security properties in weeks — a task that historically takes expert teams years. The result indicates Carbon’s potential to unlock scalable formal verification, long considered a gold-standard approach to building secure software. Enzyme assay development : Provided with only lab notebooks and raw data, Carbon went beyond standard analysis to surface hard-to-interpret data anomalies, which it used to diagnose subtle wet lab experimental artifacts such as incomplete automated mixing in deep wells, leading to substantially improved reproducibility. Moreover Carbon improved methods to deconvolute chromatography peaks and caught trace sample carryover in research instruments, significantly accelerating the development of new assays and tightening the feedback loop between computation and the bench. Protein structure prediction: Structure prediction models like AlphaFold 3 use Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) of evolutionary relatives to help infer how amino acid chains fold. As a result they often struggle on understudied, viral, microbial, and eukaryotic proteins that have very few matches in standard databases. Working in a multi-agent setup, our researchers used Gemini 4 Carbon to autonomously discover remote homologs across petabase-scale unannotated sequence archives, environmental and viral sequence catalogs, and 3D structure databases. For example, across 7 low-homolog protein families from the CASP17 blind test set, Carbon increased the number of homologs retrieved by 40-fold on average, greatly increasing the information available to structure prediction models without need for retraining. While broader benchmarking is still underway, addressing this upstream search bottleneck potentially offers a promising path toward modeling hard-to-characterize regions of the proteome. Four weeks ago, we opened applications to give 10,000 scientists access to Argon in Google Antigravity free of charge for six months to accelerate the pace of their research, and we’ve onboarded thousands of scientists already. Today, we’re expanding access to Carbon for current and future participants, and going forward, the program will continue providing access to our latest frontier models as they become available. Applications remain open and onboarding continues on a weekly rolling basis, subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection. Progress in model safety and security With each new model release, we continue to strengthen our safety and security mitigations, agentic misuse prevention, model alignment, and harm reduction proportionately with model capability. Because Gemini 4 Carbon introduces stronger cyber capabilities we build on Argon’s strong safety and security stack to fortify robustness to misuse and prompt injection. Mitigating frontier safety misuse risks: We’ve strengthened our misuse safeguards to help ensure stronger defensive reasoning does not translate into offensive risk. In simulated cyberattack testing environments seeded with ExploitBench and CyScenarioBench, Carbon blocked 99% of attack trajectories from our adaptive red-teaming agent that can iteratively revisit its attack plans after each block. The Carbon safeguards lowered the per-attempt breach rate to just 0.8% (down from 3.1% on Argon). Our safeguards also lowered the automated cyberattack query success rate to 2.17% in Gray Swan’s testing, compared to 9.86% on Argon. And external testing by Trajectory Labs found zero new universal jailbreaks across 132 hours and over 13,000 requests. Promoting safe and aligned model interactions: When we announced Carbon, we showed significant improvements in alignment as measured by our monitor flag rates across the model’s lifecycle, as well as reductions in data fabrication. New results show that on our 375-task agentic honesty benchmark, it passed 92% of tasks (compared to 70% for Argon) — declining to fill in missing experimental data 98% of the time and flagging methodological flaws 68% of the time. Protecting users from indirect prompt injection attacks: Two weeks ago, we shared that Carbon achieved a 0% prompt injection attack success rate on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark — marking the first time that milestone has been reached. At the same time, we know that prompt injection robustness remains an area for continued improvement. Our advanced automated red teaming continues to push the limits here and has shown that models could be further improved against sophisticated attacks in some distributions. It provides the data for us to continuously advance our models’ security to the next frontier. For more details, read the full Gemini 4 Carbon Safety and Security report . Getting started with Gemini 4 Carbon Starting today, Carbon joins Argon in our family of frontier models across our products: For developers: Build with the Gemini API paid tier in AI Studio and Android Studio , and if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber, you can try it in Google Antigravity and AI Studio. For enterprises: Try it in Gemini for business via the API or model drop down, Google Antigravity, or CodeMender. For everyday users: Try Carbon starting today in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber. For scientists & researchers: Apply for a chance to get access to both Argon and Carbon via Google Antigravity’s highest usage tier free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection. For cybersecurity defenders: Apply to join the Fairwind Program to get access to Carbon for cyber on a rolling basis. title: Introducing the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark
body: Introducing the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark Nov 10, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link The Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, developed with Artificial Analysis, evaluates how agents reason across visually complex files to solve real-world knowledge work tasks. Rohan Doshi Senior Product Manager, Google DeepMind Ben Caine Principal Engineer, Google DeepMind Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X In partnership with Artificial Analysis, we're launching MKA (Multimodal Knowledge Agent) , a new benchmark built to evaluate how agents reason across visually complex files to solve real-world knowledge work tasks. Introducing MKA Most knowledge work benchmarks can be solved with text alone, without ever needing to look at an image or page layout. Yet, everyday professional work looks very different. Across many industries, day-to-day work is deeply visual — from cross-referencing architectural blueprints and tracing engineering schematics to synthesizing findings into polished decks, reports, and spreadsheets. We built MKA to measure how well agents can handle this visually complex work. To ground the benchmark in real-world workflows, we partnered with domain experts across 10 verticals and 83 occupations where day-to-day work is inherently visual. Together, these specialists — from architects and biologists to underwriters and data scientists — created MKA's 200-task evaluation set to assist them in their jobs. MKA's 10 verticals. Each task reflects a multi-step project that takes a seasoned professional three to eight hours to complete, pairing a realistic prompt and a bundle of multimodal input files with an expert-written rubric of roughly 70 yes/no checks, weighted 75% on factual accuracy and 25% on visual design. Three MKA tasks, from prompt and input files to golden output and rubric. Starting today, you can explore the benchmark and evaluate your own models on Artificial Analysis . Every model runs in the same open-source agent harness, Stirrup, with the same tools, sandbox, and turn budget. An agentic autorater built on a non-Google model grades each deliverable. It opens every file, renders pages, inspects spreadsheet formulas, and checks the work against the expert rubric. When domain experts graded model outputs themselves, they agreed with the autorater 96% of the time. To keep results meaningful, Artificial Analysis runs the 200-task evaluation set and keeps it private so the tasks can't leak into training data or be found by the model via search. We've also released a separate set of 10 public tasks on Hugging Face , so anyone can inspect the format and test their own agents. Our technical report covers the methodology and results in detail. It shows that frontier models work in very different ways. On the same tasks, the models we tested have extreme differences in efficiency, using between 30 and 130 turns on average to complete each task. We show how strong perception abilities are necessary to solve each task, and we also show how models try and fail to compensate when vision is removed. Expanding visual frontiers with Gemini 4 Carbon Gemini 4 Carbon achieves #2 in quality among the models we tested, and completes tasks at 6x lower cost on average compared to the top scoring model. Gemini 4 Carbon is on the pareto frontier of quality and price for the MKA eval. Getting started Gemini 4 Carbon is available today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio . title: 40 years of American culinary history with the James Beard Foundation
body: 40 years of American culinary history with the James Beard Foundation Nov 10, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link A new Google Arts & Culture collaboration brings 10,000 menus to life, showing how American food trends have evolved. Clare Reichenbach Chief Executive Officer, James Beard Foundation Amit Sood VP, Google Arts & Culture Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Dive into American culinary history like never before, thanks to a new partnership between the James Beard Foundation and Google Arts & Culture: Bite by Bite . For over four decades, the James Beard Foundation — a launchpad for many of today’s top chefs — has hosted dinners capturing the evolution of American cuisine. This new James Beard Foundation digital archive opens a window into that evolution, with an interactive experiment and more than 10,000 digitized menus from those dinners documenting how ingredients, trends, and values have shifted across generations. Mapping 40 years of food trends The James Beard Menu Archive makes thousands of menus easy to explore and learn from. It uses AI to analyze ingredients across decades, letting you discover how dining habits have changed, from the explosion of kale in the 2000s to the decline of foie gras. More than just lists of dishes, the menus serve as cultural time capsules, revealing what diners valued at exact moments in history, how sourcing has evolved, and how regional and global influences have reshaped American dining. Beyond the menus, the archive also features a curated story series that spotlights James Beard, “ the father of American gastronomy ,” the history of the James Beard Foundation’s New York City headquarters , and more . Listening to voices from the culinary community Regarding this project, James Beard Award–winning chef Marcus Samuelsson says that food connects diverse communities. The collaboration celebrates the people behind every plate and honors their cultures and innovations. By bringing their heritage online and opening the archive to kitchens everywhere, we hope to inspire the next generation of culinary creatives. title: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps.
body: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps. Nov 10, 2026 Today at Adobe MAX, we announced we’re expanding our partnership with Adobe. Switching between apps to edit a PDF or fine-tune an image can quickly break your focus. Our partnership will bring Adobe’s creative and productivity tools directly into the Google products you use every day. It will also bring Google’s frontier AI models into Adobe’s apps. Here’s what’s coming: Work faster with PDFs: You’ll soon have a direct pathway from Google Drive and Gmail into Adobe Acrobat, surfaced as a suggested app across both services, including an “Edit with” entry point in file previews. Create right where you search and chat: Adobe is expanding its connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise with Acrobat and additional creative tools. Adobe will also bring its creative tools to AI Mode in Google Search. Powering creatives and enterprises: Businesses will be able to use Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker agent in Gemini Enterprise — an AI assistant that helps teams design graphics, work with PDFs, and launch marketing campaigns without switching apps. Exploring editing experiences with DeepMind: Adobe and Google DeepMind will explore new editing capabilities for creative professionals, starting with an image model for Photoshop that could enable near-real-time edits.
retained_feed_body: Google and Adobe are integrating creative and productivity tools. Edit PDFs in Drive and use Adobe AI in Gemini. See what’s new in this partnership.

title: Piero Cipollone: Cash and the digital euro: two sides of the same coin
body:
Cash and the digital euro: two sides of the same coin Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date Piero Cipollone Member of the ECB's Executive Board SPEECH Cash and the digital euro: two sides of the same coin Introductory statement by Piero Cipollone, Member of the Executive Board of the ECB, at the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs of the European Parliament Brussels, 10 November 2026 It is a pleasure to be back here for the first time since the Parliament adopted its position on the Single Currency Package, and I very much welcome the broad support it received in the plenary session on 9 July. This gives a strong democratic backing to the digital euro. Let me also thank you for the considerable work and constructive dialogue that have made this progress possible. A swift conclusion of the ongoing trilogue negotiations would pave the way for the adoption of the Single Currency Package [ 1 ] by the end of the year as foreseen in the One Europe, One Market Roadmap . [ 2 ] This would give us the legal certainty needed to complete our preparations for the digital euro. It would also give certainty to the market regarding the planned date for a possible first issuance, which can be set only after the Regulation is adopted. A delay in adoption could instead postpone the introduction of the digital euro, further entrench Europe’s dependence on foreign providers, and make it more difficult for European companies to innovate and compete. Europe’s achievements in payments innovation go beyond progress on the digital euro. In September we launched Pontes, which connects market distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms with the Eurosystem’s TARGET Services. [ 3 ] The launch was widely welcomed by the market, with 18 market participants and market DLT operators onboarded on day one and many others preparing to join soon. Pontes makes the settlement of tokenised transactions in central bank money an operational reality and is a major milestone in the development of digital European capital markets. On 2 November it settled the issuance of the European Stability Mechanism’s first digitally native benchmark bond of €1 billion [ 4 ] , facilitating the shift in European tokenised finance from experimentation to adoption. While I am happy to answer any questions on Pontes, I would like to focus my remarks today on the digital euro and cash. Preparing for the digital euro pilot and first issuance We are moving ahead with preparations for the digital euro pilot. It will test the digital euro’s technical functionality, operational processes and user experience, using a beta version without legal tender status. Starting in the second half of 2027, the pilot will involve Eurosystem staff, participating payment service providers (PSPs) and selected merchants offering everyday services – for example in canteens – at the ECB and participating national central banks. We have seen strong market interest in the pilot and, in July, we announced the 36 PSPs selected to join the pilot from more than 50 applicants. [ 5 ] They include banks and non-bank providers, and cover a broad range of business models, sizes and geographical locations. We are working closely with participating PSPs to hear their views and benefit from their experience. [ 6 ] In September we opened an additional call for online and mobile merchants to join the pilot to test remote payments. The final selection of merchants will be announced early next year. [ 7 ] This collaboration with market players is essential. The digital euro must work on a technical level, but also in everyday life – for consumers, merchants and PSPs. Looking further ahead, we are planning for the digital euro rollout. On our side, we plan to ensure that all relevant use cases [ 8 ] for the digital euro are made technically available from first issuance. At the same time, feedback from market participants [ 9 ] shows that a gradual rollout would support a smooth and successful first issuance by giving them sufficient time to adapt. We are glad that the co-legislators intend to provide legal clarity on the feasibility of such a phased rollout in shops. In preparation for first issuance, we are also working more closely with the market on the digital euro innovation platform. In September we launched a new call for expression of interest, inviting private companies and organisations to explore how the digital euro can foster market innovation. [ 10 ] The next wave of activities, including testing conditional payments and exploring applications of artificial intelligence in payments, will run from January to June 2027. [ 11 ] Redesigning euro banknotes Innovation also extends to banknotes. In July we invited Europeans to share their views on ten shortlisted design proposals for the new euro banknotes based on the themes “European culture” and “Rivers and birds”. The survey received almost 10 million responses, with high participation across all euro area countries and age groups. [ 12 ] This demonstrates how deeply Europeans care about their money. The survey results will inform the ECB Governing Council’s decision on the final design concept, expected around the end of this year. At that point, we will also publish the survey results. First denominations of the new banknote series are expected to enter into circulation in the early 2030s. [ 13 ] But cash must also remain widely available and accepted in practice. We therefore support strong legislative provisions on mandatory cash acceptance, access to cash across the euro area and the resilience of cash infrastructure. Conclusion Let me conclude. In today’s uncertain geopolitical environment, timely progress on the digital euro is essential to strengthen Europe’s autonomy in payments. We are doing our part by progressing with the technical preparations. But the adoption of the legal framework is necessary to finalise the digital euro’s design and Rulebook [ 14 ] and, ultimately, to issue the digital euro. In two months’ time we will mark the 25th anniversary of euro banknotes and coins entering circulation. While cash is still widely used in shops, digital payments are growing. I therefore hope that by then we will have a strong legal framework in place: one that both safeguards the acceptance of cash and gives Europeans a digital form of cash alongside it. Thank you. The Single Currency Package includes the legislative proposal on the legal tender of euro cash and the legislative proposals establishing the legal framework for a possible digital euro. One Europe, One Market Roadmap of the European Parliament, the Council of the European Union and the European Commission . See ECB (2026), “ Eurosystem brings central bank money to tokenised finance ”, press release , 21 September. See Deutsche Bundesbank (2026), “ ESM is first European supranational issuer to settle DLT-based bond issuance on Eurosystem’s Pontes platform with Bundesbank and Clearstream ”, press release , 26 October. See ECB (2026), “ ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot ”, press release , 14 July. The kick-off workshop in Frankfurt in September was an important step in building a shared understanding of the work ahead. See ECB (2026), “ Digital euro pilot: PSP kick-off workshop ”, 29-30 September. See ECB (2026), “ Call for online and mobile merchants to participate in digital euro pilot now open ”, MIP News , 15 September. Including person-to-person, e-commerce and point-of-sale payments. See ERPB (2026), “ Digital euro market rollout plan discussion ”, 13 October. See ECB (2026), “ Call for expressions of interest in a new wave of digital euro innovation platform activities ”, MIP News , 28 September. The innovation work will follow two workstreams. The experimentation workstream will help the private sector develop practical features and services that enhance user experience, including electronic receipts and conditional payments. The exploration workstream will examine how emerging technologies could enhance future releases of the digital euro, for example the application of artificial intelligence in payments. See ECB (2026), “ Almost ten million people took part in ECB survey on new euro banknotes ”, press release , 23 September. See the “ Future banknotes ” page on the ECB’s website. The digital euro scheme rulebook provides a single set of rules, standards and procedures for the provision of basic digital euro payment services for payment service providers participating in the scheme. See ECB (2026), Update on the work of the digital euro scheme’s Rulebook Development Group: Sixth progress report , 6 July. title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
body: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare. Nov 10, 2026 Google Cloud has announced Gemini for healthcare , an AI solution engineered to unify fragmented clinical, operational, and administrative systems. Moving beyond simple information retrieval, it enables healthcare teams to turn siloed data into coordinated action. Clinicians lose nearly 28 hours each week to paperwork and administrative tasks, fueling burnout and straining budgets. By integrating specialized skills and data connectors with existing third-party systems, the platform brings together critical information from electronic health records, billing platforms, clinical guidelines, and Medicare datasets. Gemini for healthcare reasons across this context to orchestrate and execute complex, multi-step workflows — such as medical records synthesis and prior authorization review — within defined guardrails and with appropriate human oversight. Initially available in preview alongside launch partners including HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health, and Northwell Health, it resolves bottlenecks and reclaims valuable staff time for patient care. Learn more on the Cloud blog .
retained_feed_body: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare to unify clinical data and automate workflows. Reduce administrative burnout. See how it works.

title: Mexican National Pleads Guilty to Possession With Intent to Distribute Heroin
body: Press Release Mexican National Pleads Guilty to Possession With Intent to Distribute Heroin Tuesday, November 10, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada RENO – A Mexican national pleaded guilty today to possession with intent to distribute nearly two pounds of heroin. “Heroin is a highly addictive, destructive poison that destroys lives, tears families apart, and fuels a wave of fatal overdoses across our nation,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “By taking this trafficker off the streets, we have cut off a pipeline of a deadly narcotic and sent a clear message to those who profit from addiction: federal law enforcement will find you, dismantle your operation, and ensure you face the full weight of justice.” “Heroin continues to pose a severe public health threat, inflicting widespread harm on families and communities,” said Brandon Lesky, Assistant Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Las Vegas District Office. “DEA is in lockstep with our HSTF partners, committed to cracking down on illicit drug trafficking and holding criminals accountable. No matter the quantity, any drug trafficker on our radar will be pursued.” According to court documents and statements made in court, on or about April 9, 2024, Juan Luis Curiel-Carrillo possessed 800 grams of heroin with the intent to distribute. Heroin is a Schedule I controlled substance. Curiel-Carrillo pleaded guilty to two counts of possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance. He faces a statutory minimum penalty of five years in prison and a statutory maximum penalty of 40 years in prison. Sentencing is scheduled on February 16, 2027, before United States District Judge Anne R. Traum. The DEA investigated this case. Assistant United States Attorney Steven Rose is prosecuting the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. ### Updated November 10, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Nevada
retained_feed_body: RENO – A Mexican national pleaded guilty today to possession with intent to distribute nearly two pounds of heroin.

title: New York Man Sentenced to Over 10 Years in Prison for Laundering Proceeds for Elder Fraud Scam Network
body: Press Release New York Man Sentenced to Over 10 Years in Prison for Laundering Proceeds for Elder Fraud Scam Network Tuesday, November 10, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona TUCSON, Ariz. – Ivan Wilbur Seales, 58, a resident of New York and citizen of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, was sentenced on Nov. 6, by United States District Judge Scott H. Rash, to 121 months in prison. Seales was previously found guilty by a jury for Conspiracy to Commit Money Laundering. As part of his sentence, Seales was also ordered to pay approximately $855,000 in restitution to the numerous victims who suffered a loss. Seales laundered nearly $1 million in proceeds for a fraud scheme network that preyed on elderly victims from around the country, including Arizona. Seales kept a portion of the ill-gotten gains and helped the scammers launder other fraudulent proceeds through a maze of financial transactions he conducted through shell companies, crypto transfers, cash withdrawals, and other financial transfers offshore. The scam targeted elderly victims with “phishing attacks” such as pop-ups and websites that impersonated trusted entities like banks and tech companies. These victims were directed to call other scammers who falsely represented they were representatives of legitimate companies such as Apple or Microsoft. Some victims received a “phishing” email or text message indicating that they had received a charge on their account from the Geek squad, PayPal, or an Anti-Virus Software company. These charges never occurred and were sent to the victims by the fraudsters to lure the victims into the scheme. Once the victims called the fraudsters, they were led to believe that these “legitimate companies” erroneously transferred an “over-refunded amount” to the victims’ bank accounts. As instructed, victims then transferred their own money back to the scammers believing that they were returning the scammers the “over-refunded amounts.” Victims were also lied to and informed that their bank accounts had been hacked or were compromised. At least one victim was told his account was linked to child pornography. To further the scam, the fraudsters directed the victims to transfer their money to various locations to “protect” their accounts or to “catch” the scammers. The United State Postal Inspection Service and New York State Police conducted the investigation. Various other State or local law enforcement agencies also provided support for the investigation. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, Tucson, handled the prosecution. CASE NUMBER:            24-CR-0419-TUC-SHR RELEASE NUMBER:    2026-188_Seales # # # For more information on the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, visit http://www.justice.gov/usao/az/ Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, on Twitter @USAO_AZ for the latest news. Contact Public Affairs Esther J. Winne Telephone: (602) 514-7740 Esther.Winne@usdoj.gov Updated November 10, 2026 Topics Elder Justice Fraud Component USAO - Arizona Press Release Number: 2026-188_Seales
