title: November 9, 2026 - FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk For Immediate Release: November 09, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (a stroke caused by a clot that did not originate in the heart) or a high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA), often called a “mini-stroke.” “Stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in the United States, and survivors are at risk of having another stroke,” said Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., MMSc, Director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Today’s approval represents a meaningful advance for patients and health care providers seeking a new option for secondary stroke prevention.” The effectiveness of Sunharbo was demonstrated in the OCEANIC-STROKE study , a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study that enrolled 12,327 adults. Participants had a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale ≤15) or high-risk TIA and were randomly assigned to Sunharbo or placebo within 72 hours of symptom onset. Both groups also received antiplatelet therapy. Sunharbo 50 mg once daily significantly reduced the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% compared to placebo over a median treatment of 14.2 months. The overall rate of major bleeding was similar between the Sunharbo and placebo groups but was increased with Sunharbo in patients older than 75 years and during the first 90 days of treatment. Gastrointestinal bleeding occurred more commonly with Sunharbo compared to placebo. The most frequently reported adverse reaction (occurring in 3% or greater of Sunharbo-treated patients) was diarrhea. Concomitant use with medicines that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (such as carbamazepine) is not recommended because these medicines may decrease Sunharbo’s effectiveness. Sunharbo is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Sunharbo should be withheld at least 24 hours before elective surgery or invasive procedures and for at least 24 hours after thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke. Sunharbo is not approved for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. The FDA granted Sunharbo Fast Track and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc., Whippany, N.J. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: FATF Recognizes Effectiveness of U.S. AML/CFT System, Advances Key Illicit Finance Initiatives
body: November 6, 2026 PARIS —Last week, senior Treasury officials led a U.S. government delegation to the Financial Action Task Force’s(FATF) plenary meetings.  The FATF, the global standard-setting body for countering money laundering, terror financing, and proliferation financing, concluded its first Plenary under the United Kingdom presidency.  The FATF adopted the Mutual Evaluation Reports of the United States and Mexico, reiterated the call to impose countermeasures on Iran, agreed to publish a new report on scam centers, and agreed to accelerate global implementation of digital asset-related standards. STOPPING IRANIAN ILLICIT FINANCE Iran remains on the FATF’s blacklist, and the FATF called upon all nations to implement reimposed United Nations Security Council Resolutions related to Iran’s ongoing lack of compliance with its nuclear agreements. The FATF also reminded all jurisdictions to impose countermeasures on Iran to restrict correspondent banking, digital asset transactions, and business relationships with Iran. DISMANTLING SOUTHEAST ASIAN SCAM COMPOUNDS The FATF also adopted a landmark report examining the financial flows fueling scam compounds, laying the groundwork for a stronger, more coordinated global response to fraud.  Building on these findings, the FATF will advance concrete measures to use its full range of tools to drive more decisive action to disrupt these criminal networks, hold jurisdictions accountable for failing to address these risks, and protect victims and the global financial system.  Scams orchestrated at these compounds often target older and vulnerable Americans, and the Trump Administration has taken numerous sanctions actions to stop the fraud. ADVANCING THE DIGITAL ASSETS SECTOR The FATF also agreed to launch a targeted review of certain jurisdictions with longstanding deficiencies related to the virtual assets sector that heighten illicit finance risks.  This review will outline decision points for the next FATF plenary on what the FATF can do to ensure accountability for jurisdictions with systemic weaknesses that enable fraudsters, drug traffickers, and proliferators to launder funds through exchanges. Click here to read the Outcomes of the FATF Plenary, 6 November 2026. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Sanctions Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses Enabling Iranian Regime
body: November 6, 2026 Several of the Targets Also Worked with Narcotrafficker and Former Olympic Snowboarder Ryan Wedding WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight money services businesses based in Canada that enable the Iranian regime, sanctioned entities associated with the regime, and other illicit actors that move assets into and out of Iran.  These companies facilitate the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets to enable international transactions involving Iran.  Many of these businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). “Canada cannot be a safe haven for illicit financial facilitators that provide sanctions evasion services to the Iranian regime and its proxies,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will pursue and disrupt the Iranian regime’s financial channels anywhere in the world.” In August, Treasury launched Operation Economic Outcast to sever the economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime and its IRGC, including Tehran’s exploitation of cryptocurrency as a tool of choice for sanctions evasion.  Today’s designations are a continuation of Treasury’s comprehensive campaign to disrupt the regime’s exploitation of digital assets to fund terrorism, human rights abuses, and attacks on U.S. personnel and allies.  These designations also follow previous OFAC sanctions on digital asset exchanges that have moved digital assets abroad on behalf of the Iranian regime, including the June 2, 2026 designations of Iranian exchanges Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex , and the August 7, 2026 designations of Aban Tether Exchange and SHPS Shelbit (Shelbit), which operates the Shelbit Exchange that has moved millions of dollars on behalf of the IRGC. Today’s action was coordinated with the Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and FINTRAC, Canada’s financial intelligence unit.  This action is also taken in coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and reflects the Trump Administration’s whole-of-government effort to combat the illicit use of digital assets for drug trafficking.  Several of the entities designated in this action have also worked with the OFAC-sanctioned Canadian drug trafficker Ryan Wedding .  Wedding has used money exchange businesses in the Vancouver and Toronto areas to launder billions of dollars in drug proceeds.  He has used couriers to transport bulk cash to those firms, which convert the funds to digital assets to send abroad.  Wedding was apprehended in January 2026 , but he worked with several of the money services businesses designated today to transfer millions of dollars’ worth of digital assets prior to being taken into U.S. custody. Today’s designations are imposed pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian digital asset sector among other key sectors of the Iranian economy.  The Department of the Treasury will continue to target not only the Iranian digital asset ecosystem, but also international entities and actors that help facilitate it.  For more information on sanctions risk associated with Iranian digital asset exchanges, please see FAQ 1250 and FAQ 1257 . CANADIAN MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES: AN IRANIAN SANCTIONS EVASION CHANNEL Canada is home to hundreds of money services businesses that enable the movement of funds into and out of Iran, both through cash-based value transfer systems and by converting cash into digital assets to send across borders.  The entities designated in this action allow sanctioned Iranian entities to use their services, thereby providing the Iranian regime with financial lifelines and the ability to continue to finance terrorism and proxy groups.  Many of these entities also receive and launder funds associated with other criminal activity.  Although Canadian and international media sources have highlighted the sanctions evasion and terrorist financing-related risks that certain of these money services businesses pose, the entities designated today remain operational.  Several of these entities have changed their business names and addresses in an attempt to evade detection and enforcement actions. Diverse Trade Inc, doing business as Million Exchange , is an Ontario-based money services business that advertises the ability to exchange Iranian rials for other currencies, as well as the management of digital assets for customers.  Digital asset addresses associated with Million Exchange have sent the equivalent of hundreds of thousands of dollars to addresses associated with the IRGC or other terrorism-related addresses.  Million Exchange has also laundered drug proceeds by using cash generated from drug sales to purchase digital assets to send back to drug dealers.  Wedding has laundered drug proceeds through Million Exchange using this method, and has also directed sending certain digital assets abroad that Million Exchange purchased with drug-related cash. 1380079 BC Limited is a British Columbia-based money services business that does business as Amin Exchange and that facilitates currency transfers between Iran and Canada, as well as the purchase and sale of digital assets. Top PC Technician Inc , which is a closely associated affiliate of 1380079 BC Limited, operates in Ontario as a money services business and also does business as the same Amin Exchange.  Digital asset addresses associated with Amin Exchange have received hundreds of thousands of dollars from Shelbit.  Amin Exchange has laundered millions of dollars in drug proceeds in Canada at locations in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal.  Amin Exchange in Vancouver has laundered drug proceeds for Wedding.  The company has received the proceeds in cash and transferred them into digital assets, which Wedding has directed to be sent abroad. NIA Nations Currency Ltd ( NIA Nations ) is a British Columbia-based money services business that advertises digital asset exchange services and the ability to transfer money from Iran to Canada.  Digital asset addresses associated with NIA Nations have transacted with addresses associated with the IRGC and sanctioned Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges, including Nobitex, Wallex, Ramzinex, and Bitpin. 2397639 Ontario Ltd, doing business as Farah Exchange , advertises itself as an Iranian exchange operating in Canada, offering foreign exchange and digital assets.  A digital asset address associated with Farah Exchange has conducted hundreds of thousands of dollars’ worth of transactions with sanctioned Iran-related exchanges Shelbit and Wallex.  Farah Exchange has also sent thousands of dollars in digital assets to addresses associated with terrorism and millions of dollars in digital assets to addresses associated with Wedding. CCC Inc and B Galaxy Inc are two Ontario companies that operate in the same location and provide currency exchange and digital asset exchange services.  A CCC Inc website offers the buying and selling of digital currencies, and indicates it is licensed in Iran and Canada.  A digital asset address associated with CCC Inc has received hundreds of thousands of dollars in digital assets from addresses associated with terrorism.  B Galaxy Inc, doing business as Cryptoyal, advertises unlimited amounts of digital assets in exchange for Iranian currencies. Darvish Exchange is an Ontario-based money services business that advertises the ability to exchange Bitcoin for Iranian rials.  A digital asset address associated with Darvish Exchange has transacted with sanctioned Iranian exchanges Nobitex, Wallex, Aban Tether Exchange, and Shelbit. OFAC is designating Million Exchange, 1380079 BC Limited, Top PC Technician Inc, NIA Nations, Farah Exchange, CCC Inc, B Galaxy Inc, and Darvish Exchange pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  In the case of sanctions related to Iran, OFAC is employing all available statutory, regulatory, and policy tools to resolve the persistent national emergencies posed by Iran, which has not changed its behavior to align with U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the persons designated and any property identified as blocked property today.

title: Operation Economic Outcast Severs MEXC Global’s Access to the U.S. Financial System
body: November 6, 2026 CVC Exchanger Facilitated at Least $16 Billion in Illicit Finance, Including for IRGC-Qods Force WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an order effectively cutting off MEXC Global’s access to the U.S. financial system. MEXC Global is a convertible virtual currency (CVC) exchanger that has facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions connected to Iranian, North Korean, and Russian sanctions evasion, as well as cybercrime, including by transacting directly with sanctioned actors. “Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.” FinCEN’s order prevents U.S. financial institutions from processing funds transfers involving MEXC Global. MEXC Global: A Hub for Sanctioned Actors MEXC Global was founded in 2018, and as of September 2026, processed more than $1 billion in daily transactions and maintained approximately $5 billion in reserves.  It is one of the top 20 largest CVC exchangers in the world.  The platform offers trading in more than 50 currencies and access to more than 3,000 different cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets. Although the platform claims to maintain anti-money laundering (AML) and customer identification and verification policies—and explicitly prohibits use by or on behalf of individuals in certain jurisdictions, including Iran and North Korea—severe deficiencies in its AML controls have allowed it to facilitate transactions for individuals or entities in those prohibited jurisdictions, making it a significant conduit for illicit finance. Between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global facilitated the movement of at least $16 billion in funds connected to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and other illicit activity.  This includes nearly $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million in direct transactions with U.S.-, EU-, and UK-sanctioned entities, making MEXC Global of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.  In fact, MEXC Global was still processing transactions with sanctioned Russian entity Garantex, and its successor Grinex, as recently as June 2026—more than four years after Garantex’s April 2022 designation by Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).  MEXC Global also facilitated at least $26 million in transactions benefitting the Russia-based, OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions evasion network and processed almost $200 million in transactions connected to the A7A5 stablecoin, a store of value used by the A7 Network to help clients evade sanctions. MEXC Global has not only facilitated Russian illicit finance but has also served as a hub for other types of illicit financial activity, including Iranian and DPRK sanctions evasion, ransomware and scam payments, and Russian and other darknet market activity.  Between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global had sent or received approximately $1 billion in direct transactions with more than 40 identified Iranian CVC exchangers, some of which are subject to U.S. and international sanctions.  In the same period, MEXC Global facilitated approximately $22 million in transactions for the OFAC- and EU-sanctioned Central Bank of Iran and the OFAC-, UK-, and EU-sanctioned Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its Qods Force. IMPLICATIONS OF TODAY’S ACTION Today’s action will protect the U.S. financial system from the significant illicit finance threats posed by MEXC Global.  The order, issued pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, prohibits U.S. financial institutions from engaging in any transmittal of funds from or to MEXC Global.  Violations of this order may result in civil or criminal penalties.  The order does not modify existing obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act (including Suspicious Activity Report filing requirements) or sanctions administered by OFAC.  The order is effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register . Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  As highlighted in FinCEN’s recent Bulletin , this includes information about violations of the Bank Secrecy Act or OFAC-administered sanctions programs that may involve the use of Iranian proxies and facilitators operating outside of Iran. FinCEN’s order can be found here . For questions about FinCEN’s order, please contact FinCEN at http://www.fincen.gov/contact . ###

title: READOUT: Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent’s Call with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng
body: November 6, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and United States Trade Representative Jameison Greer spoke with Vice Premier He Lifeng of the People’s Republic of China to discuss the bilateral economic relationship and implementation of the Busan arrangement. The two officials reaffirmed the value of maintaining direct and candid communication. Secretary Bessent emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments made in Busan and raised concerns about recent Chinese actions. He underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the United States will closely assess China’s implementation of the arrangement. Secretary Bessent reiterated the Trump Administration’s commitment to pursuing trade and economic policies that benefit American workers, farmers, and businesses and strengthen U.S. economic and national security. ###

title: November 5, 2026 - FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
body: FDA News Release FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma For Immediate Release: November 05, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. HNSCC is an aggressive, life-threatening disease for which there is a high unmet need for effective therapies. Rybrevant Faspro is not indicated as a treatment for patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is associated with human papillomavirus (HPV). Approval was based on trial results showing that more than double the percentage of patients responded to the drug compared to currently approved therapies. This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy. “Today’s approval represents a meaningful step forward for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, a disease where treatment options have historically been limited and outcomes remain poor,” said Angelo De Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “This therapy offers patients and their physicians a new option with the potential to make a real difference in people’s lives.” The Accelerated Approval Program allows for earlier approval of drugs that treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need based on surrogate or intermediate endpoints. In this case, accelerated approval of Rybrevant Faspro was granted based on overall response rate and duration of response. Since it is not yet confirmed whether this will translate into a clinically meaningful benefit in long-term outcomes, the FDA has required confirmatory studies to verify and describe clinical benefit. In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%, meaning these patients saw their tumor either decrease in size or disappear. Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less and poor outcomes. The prescribing information for use as a single agent includes warnings and precautions for hypersensitivity and administration-related reactions, interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis, dermatologic adverse reactions, ocular toxicity, and harm to an unborn baby. The FDA granted Rybrevant Faspro Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication. The approval was granted to Janssen Biotech, Inc. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: National Republican Congressional Committee v. Brown
Treasury, IRS Announce Opportunity Zones Designations for Over 6,500 Communities Across America
body: November 5, 2026 The Working Families Tax Cuts Created a Permanent Process for States to Direct More Capital to Overlooked Communities WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today announced the Qualified Opportunity Zone (QOZ) designations for all 50 states, territories, and the District of Columbia. Under President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts, the Opportunity Zone tax incentive was permanently renewed, enhanced incentives for investment in eligible rural communities were added, and a process was established for redesignating zones every ten years. The new QOZ designations will become effective on January 1, 2027, and retain this designation for ten years. “Under President Trump’s leadership, the Working Families Tax Cuts permanently renewed and strengthened Opportunity Zones, giving investors, entrepreneurs, and local leaders the long-term certainty they need to commit capital to communities that have been overlooked for too long,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Today’s announcement of the new designations will help direct private investment to these communities, expand economic opportunity, support job creation, and unlock long-term growth in these communities across the country.” “Thanks to the leadership of President Trump, Qualified Opportunity Zones were permanently extended and expanded by the Working Families Tax Cuts giving states an opportunity to attract long-term investment into underserved, rural, and economically distressed areas,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano . “By designating thousands of new Qualified Opportunity Zones, the IRS and Treasury are enabling targeted investment and growth in communities where it is needed the most.” Background Under President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts, the permanent renewal of the Opportunity Zone tax incentives, including enhanced incentives for investment in eligible rural communities, will continue to drive private investment in some of America’s most distressed communities. This builds on more than $110 billion in private-sector investment made since these tax incentives were established by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017. The full list and map of designated Opportunity Zones are available here . On April 6, Treasury and the IRS released a list of 25,332 eligible census tracts across the country for nomination, of which 8,334 are in rural areas eligible for increased benefits as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts. On July 1, Treasury and the IRS began accepting nominations from Governors and the Mayor of the District of Columbia for eligible census tracts. An additional 130 eligible census tracts, of which 28 were in rural areas, were nominated during the statutory window. In total, 6,576 eligible census tracts were nominated by the end of the statutory window, of which 2,594 are in rural areas. All of the 6,576 eligible census tracts have been designated as QOZs effective January 1, 2027. Designation as a QOZ can help these 6,576 communities across the country attract new investment, create jobs, stimulate economic growth, and provide meaningful opportunities for residents. Additional information on nomination procedures was sent directly to the Governors and Mayor of the District of Columbia. The list of eligible census tracts is available here . The poverty rate and median family income for each tract can be found here . ###

title: Treasury Targets Global Scam Networks and the Corporate Infrastructure That Enables Them
body: November 5, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 41 entities that support the business network of Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO) previously sanctioned by the United States for its role in cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and human trafficking.  Additionally, OFAC designated a Malaysian individual who defrauded U.S. victims by managing a network of Africa-based scammers. “Cyber scam syndicates continue to steal billions of dollars from American victims while relying on sophisticated international business networks to launder their illicit proceeds,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “Treasury remains committed to dismantling every layer of these organizations—from their leadership to the corporate structures and financial facilitators that enable them to operate with impunity.” Today’s action builds on OFAC’s October 14, 2025 and June 23, 2026 designations targeting Prince Group leadership, affiliated companies, and financial facilitators. Prince Group TCO-affiliated actors have generated billions of dollars in illicit proceeds through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, including digital asset investment scams, romance scams, and other online fraud that have victimized Americans and individuals around the world.  Many of these operations have been linked to scam compounds in Southeast Asia that rely on trafficked and coerced workers, while criminal proceeds are laundered through complex networks of offshore companies and financial facilitators.  The newly designated individuals and entities have helped sustain Prince Group TCO’s illicit global operations after the October 2025 and June 2026 designations by managing offshore corporate structures, concealing beneficial ownership, facilitating commercial activities, and providing administrative and financial services to senior Prince Group TCO executives.  Individuals targeted today have participated in activities to evade previous sanctions targeting the Prince Group TCO, including the transfer of property and owning of companies with or on behalf of previously designated Prince Group TCO leaders.  Today’s action further targets the corporate and financial infrastructure that has enabled Prince Group TCO leaders to conceal assets, evade prior sanctions, and maintain access to the international financial system. These actions are in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  OFAC is designating 45 targets pursuant to E.O. 13581 (“Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations”), as amended by E.O. 13863 (“E.O. 13581, as amended”), and one target pursuant to E.O. 13694 (“Blocking the Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities”), as further amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”). These actions are in coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York and Honolulu Field Offices, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the U.S. Attorney’s office for the District of Alaska.  OFAC also appreciates the cooperation of the British Virgin Islands Financial Investigation Agency (BVI FIA) and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), whose timely assistance and information sharing were instrumental in supporting this sanctions action. TARGETING THOSE WHO EXPLOIT AMERICANS THROUGH FRAUD Prince Group TCO-affiliated actors have targeted victims in the United States and around the world through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, including digital asset investment scams, romance scams, and other online financial fraud.  These schemes rely on deception and social engineering to persuade victims to transfer funds or digital assets to criminally controlled accounts, generating billions of dollars in illicit proceeds. Many of these operations are carried out from large-scale scam compounds in Southeast Asia, where trafficked and coerced workers are forced to perpetrate online fraud against victims across the globe.  Criminal proceeds are subsequently laundered through an international network of shell companies, offshore holding companies, financial facilitators, and digital asset transactions, allowing transnational criminal organizations to conceal the origin of illicit funds and integrate them into the legitimate financial system. Today’s action builds on Treasury’s ongoing efforts to dismantle not only the leadership of these criminal enterprises, but also the overseas corporate infrastructure and professional facilitators that enable them to target American victims, move illicit proceeds across jurisdictions, and evade law enforcement.  The Prince Group TCO has developed an extensive network of companies spanning multiple jurisdictions to support its commercial interests and conceal assets connected to its criminal enterprise.  Rather than operating through a single corporate structure, senior Prince Group TCO executives have relied on layers of offshore holding companies, foreign entities, nominee directors, and corporate service providers to maintain control over assets while obscuring beneficial ownership.  Today’s designations target key components of that network, including companies and individuals that have facilitated corporate administration, managed offshore entities, and provided business services to senior Prince Group TCO officials.  These facilitators have played an important role in enabling the Prince Group TCO to access the international financial system and preserve the appearance of legitimate commercial activity. DISMANTLING THE PRINCE GROUP’S CORPORATE INFRASTRUCTURE Qiu Yong is a key Prince Group TCO member who controls multiple BVI and Hong Kong companies on behalf of Prince Group TCO, and who has served as an employee of a company controlled by Prince Group TCO’s leader, Chen Zhi.  Chen Zhi was designated on October 14, 2025. Qiu Yong holds passports from multiple jurisdictions, including Cambodia, St. Lucia, and Türkiye, and is the beneficial owner of multiple BVI-based companies that control a network of Hong Kong companies involved in money lending and other business ventures. Hong Kong-based companies Premium Financial Limited (Premium Financial) and Solar Scape Financial Limited (Solar Scape Financial) are money lending companies ultimately owned by Qiu Yong through BVI-registered Sun Speed Holdings Limited (Sun Speed Holdings) and Solar Scape Limited (Solar Scape), respectively.  Hong Kong-based Direct Astute HK Limited (Direct Astute HK) is ultimately owned by Qiu Yong via BVI-registered Direct Astute Limited (Direct Astute).  Hong Kong-based Glad Vast Limited (Glad Vast), Glad Sparkle Limited (Glad Sparkle), and Glad Harvest Limited (Glad Harvest) are linked to the wine industry and are ultimately owned by Qiu Yong through BVI-registered Glad Glory Limited (Glad Glory). Per Hong Kong media reporting, Qiu was involved in the distribution and sale of wine across Hong Kong and Macao, illustrating Prince Group TCO’s reach into ostensibly legitimate businesses.  Qiu is also the beneficial owner of BVI-registered shelf companies Victory Flora Limited (Victora Flora), Win Applause Limited (Win Applause), Celestial Drive Limited (Celestial Drive), and Sino Sagacious Limited (Sino Sagacious). Hong Kong-based Zhao Mengyao , a.k.a. Amy Zhao, is Qiu Yong’s personal assistant and serves as company secretary and co-director of multiple Hong Kong-based companies ultimately controlled by Qiu Yong.  Zhao Mengyao and Qiu Yong are both shareholders of Hong Kong-based Mighty Divine Trust Hong Kong Limited (Mighty Divine Trust), a company directed by Zhou Yun, an individual previously identified by OFAC as a financial assistant and wealth manager for Prince Group TCO leader Chen Zhi.  Mighty Divine Trust and Zhou Yun were both designated on October 14, 2025. Qiu Yong is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Prince Group TCO.  Premium Financial, Solar Scape Financial, Sun Speed Holdings, Solar Scape, Direct Astute HK, Direct Astute, Glad Vast, Glad Sparkle, Glad Harvest, Glad Glory, Victora Flora, Win Applause, Celestial Drive, and Sino Sagacious are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Qiu Yong.   Zhao Mengyao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Qiu Yong. OFAC is also targeting two individuals who are holding property for, or co-directing companies with, Prince Group TCO executive Chen Bo, who was designated on June 23, 2026. This includes Chen Bo’s wife, Cambodian national He Yujing , and Cambodian Prince Group TCO associate Visal Pang . Since OFAC’s action in October 2025, Chen Bo has transferred ownership of his Tokyo mansion to He Yujing, who also owns the Cambodian company Super Light Speed Kh Technology Co., Ltd .  Cambodia-based Visal Pang controls eleven Cambodian companies, several of which he co-directs with Chen Bo: Cambodia First Unite Construction Group (CFU Group) Co., Ltd., First Unite International Logistics Co., Ltd., First Unite Networks Entertainment Co., Ltd., First Unite Property Co., Ltd., First Unite Decoration (Cambodia) Co., Ltd., Cambodian First Unite Construction Machinery Co., Ltd., Linkedus Technology Co., Ltd., Cambo Duty Free Merchandise Co., Ltd., Marco Polo Hotel Co., Ltd., U-Life Go Now Co., Ltd. , and U-Life Kh Super App Co., Ltd. Visal Pang was also designated by the United Kingdom on March 26, 2026. Chen Bo remains in control of eleven Cambodian companies: Asian Welfare Lotteries Co., Ltd. , CB General Insurance PLC. , Cambodian Resource Energy Development Co., Ltd. , Cambodian Unite Wei Ye Investment Co. , DT Zhi Zao, Co., Ltd. , First Aquatic Industrial Co., Ltd. , Mo Net Beauty Co., Ltd. , Prince International Airlines Co., Ltd. , Richeng Property Developer Co., Ltd. , Tian Xu International Technology Plc. , and ZHX Printing Equipment Cambodia Co., Ltd . He Yujing is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of Prince Group TCO.  Super Light Speed Kh Technology Co., Ltd is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, He Yujing. Visal Pang is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of Prince Group TCO.  Cambodia First Unite Construction Group (CFU Group) Co., Ltd., First Unite International Logistics Co., Ltd., First Unite Networks Entertainment Co., Ltd., First Unite Property Co., Ltd., First Unite Decoration (Cambodia) Co., Ltd., Cambodian First Unite Construction Machinery Co., Ltd., Linkedus Technology Co., Ltd., Cambo Duty Free Merchandise Co., Ltd., Marco Polo Hotel Co., Ltd., U-Life Go Now Co., Ltd., and U-Life Kh Super App Co., Ltd. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Visal Pang. Asian Welfare Lotteries Co., Ltd., CB General Insurance PLC., Cambodian Resource Energy Development Co., Ltd., Cambodian Unite Wei Ye Investment Co., DT Zhi Zao, Co., Ltd., First Aquatic Industrial Co., Ltd., Mo Net Beauty Co., Ltd., Prince International Airlines Co., Ltd., Richeng Property Developer Co., Ltd., Tian Xu International Technology Plc., and ZHX Printing Equipment Cambodia Co., Ltd. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Chen Bo. On June 23, 2026, OFAC designated Prince Group TCO associate Dai An, a high-level leader in the Prince Group TCO.  Dai is the majority owner of Singapore-based Chen Hua Holdings Pte Ltd (Chen Hua Holdings) and serves as director for Mauritius-based Meritwise Group Public Ltd (Meritwise Group) and Malaysia-based Greenmeadows Properties Sdn Bhd (Greenmeadows). Chen Hua Holdings, Meritwise Group, and Greenmeadows are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Dai An. Singapore-based Greenbay Multi Media Pte Ltd (Greenbay Multi Media) is 100 percent owned by OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO executive Thet Li.  Thet Li was designated by OFAC on October 14, 2025. Greenbay Multi Media is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Thet Li. SANCTIONS AGAINST FACILITATOR OF MADAGASCAR-BASED SCAM NETWORK Chui Kok Wa (Chui) led an extensive network of scammers located in Madagascar that targeted Americans with scams, including defrauding Americans of digital assets.  The scammers led by Chui exploited cyber-enabled technologies, including cryptocurrencies and digital systems and technologies, to defraud numerous Americans of over $400,000 equivalent, thereby materially contributing to the cybercrime and scam center threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economic health of the United States.  Chui’s network garnered sympathy from vulnerable victims in order to misappropriate their funds for the private financial gain of his network. OFAC is designating Chui Kok Wa pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being responsible for or complicit in, or having engaged in, directly or indirectly, cyber-enabled activities originating from, or directed by persons located, in whole or in substantial part, outside the United States that are reasonably likely to result in, or have materially contributed to, a threat to the national security, foreign policy, or economic health or financial stability of the United States, and that have the purpose of or involve causing a misappropriation of funds or economic resources, intellectual property, proprietary or business confidential information, personal identifiers, or financial information for commercial or competitive advantage or private financial gain. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Global Maritime Fraud Network Supporting Iranian Regime
body: November 4, 2026 Network Circumvented Maritime Law to Enable Iran’s Shadow Fleet WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury targeted the vast criminal network of India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma and his spouse, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid , who have supported Iran’s shadow fleet through a web maritime fraud. Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies. “As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air.” False flags and fake maritime certifications allow vessels engaging in illicit activity to evade international regulations aimed at ensuring crew safety and safeguarding against environmental harm.  Falsely flagged vessels carry no valid protection and indemnity insurance, meaning that Iranian shadow fleet vessels operating under false flags could potentially cause billions of dollars in damages to the economies of the countries in whose territorial waters they operate. OFAC today also sanctioned Türkiye-based Fugo Ground Services Inc for its ongoing services in support of Iran’s aviation sector. Treasury has repeatedly warned that it will take action against those who continue to support Iran’s aviation industry, a key enabler of the regime’s destabilizing proliferation and terrorist activity. Concurrently with these designations, OFAC is issuing a new alert to industry to warn of the sanctions risks of dealing with potentially falsely flagged vessels, reemphasizing previous warnings from Treasury to the maritime industry to screen against unscrupulous actors such as Sharma and the vessels his network supports.  OFAC’s action also follows through on Treasury’s previous warning that any foreign firm or individual enabling sanctioned Iranian airlines—including through aircraft transfers, cargo services, or general sales agent support—will face serious consequences for supporting the world’s leading state sponsor of terrorism.  The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day , Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime.  Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . SHARMA CRIMINAL NETWORK For years, Suniel Kumar Sharma (Sharma) and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid (Shahid), have, through their base in Chandigarh, India, defrauded maritime regulatory administrations in multiple jurisdictions in order to establish false flagging authorities and maritime classification societies.  Purporting to represent nations from nearly every continent, from Guyana to Eswatini and Laos, Sharma and Shahid have allowed the Iranian shadow fleet, including those operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies, to evade international restrictions on their operation. Sharma and Shahid’s operations began as early as 2014, when the couple sought to impersonate the flagging authority of the Caribbean nation of Dominica.  In 2023, Sharma established the Singapore-based Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE. Ltd. (Eswatini Maritime), which, despite being publicly disavowed by Eswatini authorities, continues to provide flagging services for vessels transporting Iranian petroleum, including the sanctioned vessel PING SHUN (IMO 9231901) , which at the time of its sanctioning had engaged in multiple shipments of Iranian oil. Many of Sharma and Shahid’s false flagging registries are not tied to registered companies, however.  In each case, the Sharma network purchases web domains, creating websites that claim to offer a variety of services on behalf of a country that has not authorized it to provide any of those services.  The services often include flagging, seafarer training and certification, and vessel classification, all of which are traditionally handled by legitimate organizations that hold vessels to strict international standards. Sharma’s network can be tied to multiple active websites that purport to belong to legitimate flagging registries.  Among these false representations are websites purporting to provide flagging services on behalf of Aruba, Guyana, Mali, Mozambique, Malawi, Sint Maarten, and Timor-Leste, among others.  Sanctioned shadow fleet vessels have since gravitated towards these registries despite widespread awareness that they are not endorsed by the relevant governments.  For example, on April 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of War seized the false Guyana-flagged MAJESTIC X, formerly known as the PHONIX (IMO 9198317), which was carrying Iranian oil at the time of its boarding. Sharma and Shahid additionally manage a network of primarily India-based entities, some of which are used to establish fraudulent flagging registries.  Sharma is the managing director of India-based Oceaniek Technologies India , a company he has used to establish duplicitous flag registries, including those purporting to belong to Aruba, Nicaragua, and Sint Maarten.  Through these fraudulent registries Sharma has provided false flags to numerous sanctioned vessels that transport Iranian petroleum products, including LATTAFA (IMO 9245794), BINARY STAR (IMO 9380570) , and VERA (IMO 9304655) . As Sharma’s activities have garnered greater attention, Shahid has stepped in to manage—at least on paper—the pair’s business empire, which includes companies ranging from financial services businesses to media streaming platforms.  Following press coverage of his activities, Sharma has closed down multiple deceitful registries, including the Laos Ship Registry and Maritime Safety Administration, previously known as the International Maritime Safety Agency of Guyana, a company that served as a false flagging agency for Guyana and was likely intended to similarly impersonate the Laotian government. In addition to Shahid, Indian nationals Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh nominally serve as directors of Sharma’s businesses, including India-based Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited . Suniel Kumar Sharma is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.  Jaspreet Preeti Shahid is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Suniel Kumar Sharma. Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE. Ltd. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid. Oceaniek Technologies India is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Suniel Kumar Sharma. Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid.  Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited. In addition, the following India-based companies are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid: Precept Trends Private Limited ; Polynesia Maritime Private Limited ; Alexarya Finserv Private Limited ; Alexarya Media and Entertainment Private Limited ; Viharaboating Private Limited ; and Aryavart Maritime and Educational Trust . GROUND HANDLING COMPANY SUPPORTING IRANIAN AIRLINES On August 24, 2026, Treasury issued determinations pursuant to E.O. 13902 against critical sectors––including aviation––that the Iranian regime uses to try to prop up its economy.  As Treasury has repeatedly highlighted, Iran uses its supposed “commercial” airlines, many of which are controlled by the regime and its military, to ferry fighters, ship weapons and sensitive technologies, and move gold and cash to its proxies.  Today, OFAC is taking action against a Türkiye-based ground handling company that continues to service sanctioned Iranian airlines, despite Treasury’s warnings of the sanctions risks associated with supporting Iran’s aviation sector. Türkiye-based Fugo Ground Services Inc provides ground handling and other services to several U.S.-designated Iranian airlines that continue to fly to Türkiye.  Fugo Ground Services Inc has direct service agreements with U.S.-sanctioned Iranian carriers including Iran Air Tour, Saha Airlines, Sepehran Airlines, Varesh Airlines, Taban Airlines, and Ata Airlines Company, and began providing services to several of these carriers in the weeks after their September 8, 2026 designations . OFAC is designating Fugo Ground Services Inc pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the aviation sector of the Iranian economy. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions, unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades or conspires to violate U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  Financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons, including the persons designated today.  This includes, in addition to blocking prohibitions, that OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  In the case of sanctions related to Iran, OFAC is employing all available statutory, regulatory, and policy tools to resolve the persistent national emergencies posed by Iran, which has not changed its behavior to align with U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List. Click here for more information on the persons designated today. ###
